items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to establishing a school voter
registration access program for students in grades ten, eleven, and twelve;
and to amend the election law, in relation to providing for a school voter
registration access program for students in grades ten, eleven, and twelve
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5073

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
establishing a school voter registration access program for students in
grades ten, eleven, and twelve; and to amend the election law, in
relation to providing for a school voter registration access program for
students in grades ten, eleven, and twelve

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To implement procedures pursuant to Chapter 2 of the Laws of 2019
regarding voter registration and pre-registration for eligible high
school students in New York State.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Establishes a new Article 25 entitled the School Voter Regis-
tration Access Program in education law requiring school districts,
boards of cooperative educational services, charter schools, and non-
public schools to adopt a policy to promote student voter registration
and preregistration pursuant to chapter 2 of the laws of 2019 for
students in grades ten, eleven and twelve. The policy must include at
least ten days for voter registration and pre-registration throughout
the school year and must provide students with reasonable access to the
registration and pre-registration process. The policy may include
collaboration with county and local boards of elections and schools may
engage outside organizations to conduct the voter registration and pre-
registration days.

This section further provides timelines and procedures for conducting
voter registration and pre-registration days and stipulates that
completion and submission of voter registration and pre-registration
forms is not a course requirement or graded assignment for students.

Sections 2 through 9. Adds provisions of education law pertaining to the
powers and duties of school boards, boards of cooperative educational
services, charter schools and the Chancellor of the Department of Educa-
tion in New York City to adopt policies pursuant to Article 25 estab-
lishing the School Voter Registration Access Program.

Section 10 amends the election law to provide for implementation of the
School Voter Registration Access Program and requires the state board of
elections to adopt rules and regulations to facilitate this program.

Section 11. Provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In recent years, there has been national alarm at our very low rates of
voter registration and participation. It is essential that we connect
citizens to the electoral process at a young age to educate and inform
them of the importance of participating in the voting process and that
we instill in them, at a young age, the notion that their voice matters
in the political process and in shaping society.  Academic literature
has highlighted low voting participation rates among young citizens. We
can increase the potential for qualified voters to exercise their right
to vote and become engaged in lifelong civic responsibility by providing
access to registering and pre-registering to vote in schools.
Schools have a responsibility to prepare students to be active citizens
and are uniquely situated to ensure that all students have the opportu-
nity to register to vote and to participate in the electoral process.
Too often these opportunities are not broad enough in scope to reach all
students.

In adopting a school voter registration and pre-registration access
program for students in grades 10, 11, and 12, we can improve the chanc-
es of greater participation in the voting process and promote long-term
engagement for civic responsibility and participation.  Chapter 2 of the
Laws of 2019 expressly authorized pre-registration of 16 and 17-year
olds as part of an effort to encourage voting at age 18. This bill
provides the framework to ensure all schools with students of those ages
provide the opportunity for, and in fact encourage, students to register
to vote.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date upon which it shall have become a law and shall apply to all school
years commencing on and after such effective date provided, however,
that the amendments to section 2590-h of the education law made by
section nine of this act shall not affect the expiration and reversion
of such section, when upon such date the provisions of section ten of
this act shall take effect. Effective immediately, the addition, amend-
ment and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implemen-
tation of this act on its effective date are authorized to be made on or
before such date.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5073A

SPONSOR: MAYER
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
establishing a school voter registration access program

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To implement procedures pursuant to Chapter 2 of the Laws of 2019
regarding voter registration and pre-registration for eligible high
school students in New York State.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Establishes a new Article 25 entitled the School Voter Regis-
tration Access Program in education law requiring school districts,
boards of cooperative educational services, charter schools, and non-
public schools to adopt a policy to promote student voter registration
and pre-registration pursuant to chapter 2 of the laws of 2019 for
students in grades ten, eleven and twelve. The policy shall include
procedures for acquiring and transmitting voter applications to and from
the local board of elections and dissemination among their appropriate
schools, methods of regular communication with eligible students about
the availability of the applications and their right to register to
vote. The policy may include collaboration with local boards of
elections and outside organizations to assist in making voter registra-
tion and pre-registration applications available.

This section further stipulates that completion and submission of voter
registration and pre-registration forms is not a course requirement or
graded assignment for students and that local election boards must
comply with requests for applications.

Section 2 establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In recent years, there has been national alarm at our very low rates of
voter registration and participation. It is essential that we connect
citizens to the electoral process at a young age to educate and inform
them of the importance of participating in the voting process and that
we instill in them, at a young age, the notion that their voice matters
in the political process and in shaping society. Academic literature has
highlighted low voting participation rates among young citizens. We can
increase the potential for qualified voters to exercise their right to
vote and become engaged in lifelong civic responsibility by providing
access to registering and pre-registering to vote in schools.  Schools
have a responsibility to prepare students to be active citizens and are
uniquely situated to ensure that all students have the opportunity to
register to vote and to participate in the electoral process.  Too often
these opportunities are not broad enough in scope to reach all students.

In adopting a school voter registration and pre-registration access
program for students in grades 10, 11, and 12, we can improve the chanc-
es of greater participation in the voting process and promote long-term
engagement for civic responsibility and participation. Chapter 2 of the
Laws of 2019 expressly authorized pre-registration of 16 and 17-year
olds as part of an effort to encourage voting at age 18. This bill

provides the framework to ensure all schools with students of those ages
provide the opportunity for students to register to vote.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect July 1, 2020.
